sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and setup
sections.what: Imports the argument parser, the JSON tools, and the extraction and worker functions. It also sets up multiprocessing support.
sections.why: Lets the script use the shared extraction code and run correctly when packaged.

sections.name: main
sections.title: Run extraction and print the summary
sections.what: Reads the command arguments, runs extraction either under supervision or directly, passes progress lines to the console, and prints the result without the document list.
sections.why: Likely reason: the summary keeps the output short while the full document list stays in the output files.
sections.watch_out: The supervised path reads extraction.json from the output folder, so a failed stage with no results file will raise an error here.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Command entry point
sections.what: Enables multiprocessing support and then runs the main function when the file is run directly.
sections.why: Likely reason: multiprocessing needs this setup when the program is packaged into an executable.

summary: A command-line tool that extracts the documents from an inventoried project package, either directly or under supervision, and prints a summary of the results.
purpose: Lets a developer run the package extraction step by hand and see its progress and outcome.
why: Likely reason: running extraction from the command line helps debugging without starting the whole web app.
how: It reads the inventory and output paths. With the supervised flag it runs the extraction stage through a supervisor that tracks progress in a control folder and then reads the results file. Without it, it calls the extraction function directly. It prints progress and a summary without the document list.
inputs: An inventory file from the inspection step and an output folder.
outputs: Extracted documents in the output folder, an extraction.json results file in supervised mode, and a printed summary.
risks: The summary hides the document list, so a developer must open the output folder to see the documents. Supervised mode depends on a control folder next to the output.
debug: Check the printed progress lines, then open extraction.json in the output folder. In supervised mode, look in the job control folder for stage state.
